headline: Zonneveld beats Littler 5-4, but champion reaches last 16
standfirst: Niels Zonneveld won 5-4 in Group A despite Luke Littler's 150 finish with three bullseyes, with Littler through to face Jermaine Wattimena.
body: Luke Littler's unbeaten run at the Grand Slam of Darts ended on Monday night, when Niels Zonneveld beat the defending champion 5-4 in Group A at Aldersley Leisure Village. Littler still progresses to the last 16 as one of the group's two qualifiers.

Littler had beaten Beau Greaves 5-2 in his opener, so he needed only three legs against Zonneveld to go through. He got them, but Zonneveld who had lost 5-3 to Greaves on the first night, needed to win by at least 5-2 to progress.

The Dutchman missed a match dart with the score at 5-3, and Littler then produced the moment that dominated social media. Facing a 150 finish, he hit three bullseyes in a row to force a deciding leg. Dartsnews asked whether it was the greatest checkout in darting history.
Zonneveld did not let the chance slip a second time. He won the last leg to take the match and finish second in the group.
Darts World described the defeat as the end of Littler's long unbeaten streak in Wolverhampton.

Littler's next opponent will be Jermaine Wattimena, who was the first player into the last 16. Wattimena won Group B by beating Alan Soutar 5-4 in a final leg in which he survived eight match darts against him.
